description: Saga + event sourcing + CQRS decomposed. Compensating transactions, saga state machines, event store, snapshot, projections, eventual consistency. The mechanisms by which distributed business processes maintain consistency without 2PC blocking.

sub_mechanisms.name: saga_compensation
sub_mechanisms.definition: Each forward step has compensating action that undoes it. Failure triggers compensation chain.
sub_mechanisms.why: Replaces distributed rollback. Compensation may differ from inverse (refund vs un-charge — refund creates new transaction). Designed at business level.

sub_mechanisms.name: saga_state_machine
sub_mechanisms.definition: Orchestrator tracks saga state. Transitions on events. Failure transitions to compensation chain.
sub_mechanisms.why: Explicit state model. Step failure → start compensation from current state backwards. Tools: Temporal, AWS Step Functions, Camunda.

sub_mechanisms.name: compensation_idempotency
sub_mechanisms.definition: Compensations must be idempotent. May be invoked multiple times during retry.
sub_mechanisms.why: Network failures + retries inevitable. Compensation must handle 'already compensated' case. Common pattern: check state before acting.

sub_mechanisms.name: non_compensable_actions
sub_mechanisms.definition: Some actions can't be undone (email sent, money paid out). Sagas must account for these.
sub_mechanisms.why: Pure compensation impossible. Alternatives: defer until commit, send 'oops' email, accept business loss. Saga design considers these explicitly.

sub_mechanisms.name: event_store
sub_mechanisms.definition: Append-only log of events. Source of truth for application state.
sub_mechanisms.why: Foundation of event sourcing. EventStore DB, Kafka as event store, custom on DBs. Events immutable; new events express change.

sub_mechanisms.name: event_replay
sub_mechanisms.definition: Reconstruct state by replaying events from beginning (or from snapshot).
sub_mechanisms.why: State at any time = events up to time. Time travel built in. Cost: long event chains expensive without snapshots.

sub_mechanisms.name: snapshot_optimization
sub_mechanisms.definition: Periodically save aggregate state. Replay from latest snapshot, not from beginning.
sub_mechanisms.why: Without: replay cost grows with history. With: bounded replay. Trade: storage + occasional rebuild on schema change.

sub_mechanisms.name: CQRS_command_side
sub_mechanisms.definition: Write model: receives commands; produces events; events written to event store.
sub_mechanisms.why: Optimised for write consistency. Pure event production. No read concerns. Often combined with event sourcing.

sub_mechanisms.name: CQRS_query_side
sub_mechanisms.definition: Read models: projections built from events. Multiple read models for different query patterns.
sub_mechanisms.why: Each read model optimised for its queries. Denormalised, materialised. Updated asynchronously from events. Eventually consistent with writes.

sub_mechanisms.name: projection_rebuilding
sub_mechanisms.definition: On schema change or bug fix: discard projection, rebuild from events.
sub_mechanisms.why: Event store = ground truth. Read models can be regenerated. Powerful for evolution: change projection logic + rebuild from history.

sub_mechanisms.name: outbox_pattern
sub_mechanisms.definition: DB transaction includes business write + event in outbox table. Separate process publishes from outbox.
sub_mechanisms.why: Atomicity: DB transaction commits both or neither. Decouples DB commit from message broker availability. Standard pattern for event-driven systems with relational DBs.

sub_mechanisms.name: saga_choreography_vs_orchestration
sub_mechanisms.definition: Choreography: events emitted; services react autonomously. Orchestration: central coordinator drives steps.
sub_mechanisms.why: Choreography: decoupled but flow scattered across services. Orchestration: centralised flow but coordinator critical. Choose per saga complexity.

derivation_rules.name: saga_compensations_must_be_idempotent
derivation_rules.why: Network retries → compensation may run multiple times. Refund $100 twice = wrong. Idempotency via state check or idempotency key. Foundation of safe sagas.

derivation_rules.name: event_sourcing_gives_audit_log_for_free
then: every state change is automatically auditable
derivation_rules.why: Events are the audit trail. 'How did this account get to $0?' = replay events. Financial systems + regulated industries depend on this. Difficult to retrofit; design choice.

derivation_rules.name: CQRS_read_models_eventually_consistent
if: read models update asynchronously from events
then: reads after write may see stale data
derivation_rules.why: Write commits; event published; projection processes event; read model updated. Some delay always. App must handle (display 'processing' or read-your-writes from cache).

derivation_rules.name: outbox_pattern_ensures_event_durability
if: DB write + event publication in same transaction via outbox
then: events are not lost on broker outage
derivation_rules.why: Outbox in DB transaction. Separate publisher reads outbox + publishes. Broker down: outbox accumulates; resume when up. Standard for transactional event publishing.

derivation_rules.name: orchestration_easier_to_debug_choreography_more_decoupled
derivation_rules.why: Choreography: flow is scattered events. Debugging requires reading all services. Orchestration: flow in one place (state machine). Trade-off per saga complexity.
